title: Playflow Studio: visual editor for incident playflows and automated steplets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build 'Playflow Studio', a lightweight visual authoring environment that converts operator runbooks into modular, idempotent steplets and deployable task-flows. The studio should let support engineers and SREs compose conditional steps, inject pre/post checks (circuit breakers, SLO guards), and publish versioned task flows that the ops automation runtime can execute with audit trails.

Scope: MVP focuses on incident triage/use-cases for the admin utilities team: host restarts, cache invalidation, model rollout rollback, and telemetry toggles. Editor features: drag-drop steplets, parameter schemas, simulated dry-run, YAML export, and one-click publish to the ops-runner service.

Acceptance criteria: (1) Author can create a 5-step playflow that includes branching and a manual approval gate and successfully publish it to the test namespace. (2) Published flows execute in the test environment with idempotency guarantees and produce telemetry events consumable by Console. (3) All privileged steps require a policy check and appear in audit logs. (4) Security review completed and sign-off recorded.
comments: 2026-01-26 - Kickoff: scoped MVP. Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Lina (PM), Ravi (SRE). Agreed to prioritize idempotent primitives and auditability over full feature parity with current runbooks.

2026-02-02 - Spike complete: prototype editor using React + MergoFlow. Prototype shows conditional branches and parameterized step templates. Link to prototype: https://figma.redwood.com/playflow-mvp (internal).

2026-02-05 - Security sync: discussed secrets handling for privileged steps. Decision to integrate with KMS and require short-lived delegated tokens for published flows. Action: create security checklist item for review. Assigned to: Priya (Sec).

2026-02-10 - Engineering review: Marco submitted initial backend API design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playflow/pull/142. Requested changes: add explicit run_id and reconcile strategy for retries. (Reviewer: Diego)
2026-02-14 - UX feedback from support bench: users want a 'simulate' mode that runs locally against a replayed event to validate branching. Adding to scope as low-effort win.
2026-02-18 - Infra note: must add quota/burst controls for automated flows to avoid DDOSing downstream services. Raised ENG-763560 to track rate-limiting middleware work.
decision_log: Use modular steplet model (small units with well-defined inputs/outputs) to allow reuse across playflows.
Require short-lived delegated tokens for any step that performs privileged actions; do not store long-lived secrets in flows.
MVP will export flows as YAML + metadata, and the ops-runner will accept a flow_version reference rather than raw code to ease rollbacks.
Defer advanced scheduling (cron, delayed retries) to a follow-up; initial runtime supports immediate execution + controlled retries.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): internal SREs only in dev namespace. Validate idempotency and telemetry (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (beta): support bench in staging with simulation mode enabled and manual approval gates required for privileged steps (3 weeks).
Phase 2 (gradual): limited production rollout for non-privileged flows and rate-limited automation (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (wide): enable privileged flows after security sign-off and completed audit tooling (TBD).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Automated flows could perform destructive actions if a step is misconfigured. Mitigation: add approval gates and required dry-run for any flow that includes destructive primitives.
Risk: Secret leakage from parameters. Mitigation: schema validation and enforce KMS-backed parameter references; no plain-text secrets in published YAML.
Risk: Increased load on downstream services during mass remediation runs. Mitigation: implement rate-limiting middleware and quota enforcement (tracked in ENG-763560).
